dev_agent_struggles.symptom: The migrated <Button> controls carry only a Content string plus a Click handler; none has x:Name or AutomationProperties.AutomationId. The scoring task's automated Capture-AppScenarios could not reliably invoke the Scenario 3 'Query Profile for HDR Support' button because its Content is a substring of the nav item '3) Query Profile for HDR Support' and there was no AutomationId to disambiguate (invokeOk=false; parity actionsInvoked 0/1).
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: n/a (not a build loop) — surfaced only in scoring (discrepancies.json 'automation-metadata'; parity-result.json scenario 3 actionsInvoked=0)
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: The dev-agent copied the UWP XAML verbatim (correct fidelity behaviour), and the UWP source buttons themselves had no x:Name/AutomationId. The skill's fidelity rule says 'copy verbatim, preserve names' but never says to ADD a stable AutomationId to interactive controls that lack one — so unnamed controls stay unaddressable by UIA.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Scoring fell back to manual invoke by a synthetic UIA token (btn-queryprofilefor-9f72) and confirmed the button is live; scored pass. But automated targeting would have failed → potential partial on a stricter run with no manual fallback.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: A migration rule + a Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 WARN that flags interactive controls (Button/ToggleButton/ToggleSwitch/etc.) which have neither x:Name nor AutomationProperties.AutomationId, telling the agent to add a stable AutomationId.

missing_tooling.need: A validator signal for interactive controls lacking any stable automation identifier (x:Name or AutomationId).
missing_tooling.would_have_saved: The Scenario 3 capture-targeting ambiguity; makes every migrated app reliably drivable by UIA-based parity checks and accessible to screen readers.

env_issues.workaround: Cosmetic host-theme difference, not a migration defect; UWP golden behavioural capture unavailable — judged from source. No skill action.
